# Concurrent change-groups on the same user delta-merge: each side adds a
# different group and both additions survive on top of the shared base group.

exec git init
exec git config user.email test@sesam.dev
exec git config user.name 'Sesam Test'

exec sesam init --user admin --install-merge
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'init sesam'

# Base: bob in dev.
exec sesam tell --user bob --recipient $BOB_PUBKEY --group dev
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'add bob'

# OURS: bob gains ops.
exec git checkout -b ours
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add ops
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'ours: bob += ops'

# THEIRS: bob gains sec.
exec git checkout -b theirs ours~1
exec sesam user change-groups --user bob --group-add sec
exec git add -A
exec git commit -m 'theirs: bob += sec'

# Merge: the driver merges the log and reports a conflict (exit 1) so git stops.
# (sesam.yml also conflicts - accepted for now.)
exec git checkout ours
! exec git merge theirs
stdout 'merged it automatically'

# The merged log verifies and carries both group additions (ops from ours, sec
# from theirs' delta-merged entry).
exec sesam verify --verify-mode no-disk
exec sesam show .sesam/audit/log.jsonl
stdout 'ops'
stdout 'sec'
stdout '"operation": "merge"'
